title: Cross-Sheet Invariants — 20 CSR Registry v1.0
description: Populated INSTANCE document (not a meta-schema) carrying the 20 Cross-Sheet Rules per §9.1. Top-level `rules` array is the source of truth consumed by the consistency_check tool. Per S3.5 pivot: instance documents live at `NAME.json`; if a paired meta-schema is ever needed it would go to `NAME.schema.json`. Verdict aggregation (§9.2/§17.2): any RED → RED; else any AMBER/WARN → AMBER; all PASS → GREEN. Severity-to-verdict: CRITICAL/HIGH → RED on FAIL, MEDIUM/LOW → AMBER on FAIL.
verdict_aggregation: any RED → RED; else any AMBER/WARN → AMBER; all PASS → GREEN

rules.rationale: A task targeting an unknown URL is either a typo or a dangling reference; both produce unactionable entries that corrupt the DONE cascade and pollute completed_work.
Dashboard R48 is the headline DONE-count KPI; drift means stakeholders see wrong numbers. Also mirrored as CI-06 for the 8-invariant view.
TODO count feeds the whats-next priority queue sizing; drift desynchronizes reminder thresholds.
ONGOING count gates parallelization limits; auto-repair via dashboard_refresh (§9.3).
A completed_work row referencing a non-DONE task means the DONE cascade §21.4 was partial — either master_task was reverted or the cascade aborted before step 5.
Content planned outside the topical map creates orphan pages with no pillar home — kills topical authority signal. Mirrored as CI-07.
Improvement tasks must target pages that both exist (crawl_sitemap) AND have a pillar assignment (topical_map); otherwise the edit has no strategic context.
Quick wins must be either reachable (in sitemap) or already getting impressions (GSC). A URL in neither set is fictitious.
Every cluster keyword target must have a pillar home; otherwise the cluster is orphan and cluster→pillar reporting breaks.
Cannibalization rows referencing non-crawled pages are stale; SF re-import needed before acting.
Schema audit rows for unknown URLs indicate a sitemap/crawl drift that must be resolved before schema fixes are applied.
Redirect/404 entries must be backed by actual SF response codes; fabricated rows cause redirect_chain and 404 sweep reports to double-count.
robots.txt declarations and SF-detected indexability must agree; a delta means one of the two is stale (cached robots or stale crawl).
GSC may report impressions for redirected URLs for up to 6 months; accepting sitemap-OR-redirect-target union avoids false-positive orphan flags.

rules.rule: cannibalization intent çakışması intent-matrix.json ile tutarlı
rules.rationale: Two pages ranking for the same query are only 'cannibalizing' when their intents overlap per intent-matrix.json — a product page + a blog post for the same query may be intentional. Requires manual triage per §9.3.
Pillar key drift breaks every pillar-scoped report and the pillar_launch event (§20.2). Auto-repair available (JSON re-key + user confirm §9.3).
Cluster label drift detaches keywords from their cluster definitions — downstream keyword_difficulty/priority scoring becomes meaningless.

rules.rule: url_normalizer(x) == x for every URL in every sheet
rules.rationale: Non-idempotent URLs break cross-sheet JOINs; mirrored as CI-05. Any failure means the url_normalizer was bypassed at write time (boundary violation §6.6).

rules.rule: gsc_performance URL set is consistent with dashboard KPI URL set
rules.rationale: Dashboard KPIs derived from gsc_performance must stay in sync after every mcp_feed run; drift means dashboard_refresh missed a sheet.
Stale SF data + fresh Excel date is a lying report. Freshness SLA is per-sheet in excel-source-manifest.json; staler-than-SLA triggers AMBER.

Quick-win rows must point at URLs that the opportunity sheet has already triaged (canonical 'url | action' or freeform 'Optimize <url> for query X'); orphan quick_wins indicate that the opportunity intake step was skipped (Q-V1.2-OPP-COVERAGE-01 Phase B post-closeout schema-first override 17'inci uygulama).

Severity-typed columns (priority/level/impact carrying $ref severityEnum in master-excel.schema.json) must hold one of the four canonical values; any other token corrupts severity-aware reporting and breaks the verdict aggregator.

master_task.created_date (col K) must parse as ISO 8601; Excel-cached datetimes already pass, freeform strings require fromisoformat tolerance (Z → +00:00). Non-parseable cells break time-series reporting and the DONE cascade audit trail.

rules.rule: project.config.json declares language.content_locale (nested) + market (root) per schema 1.3
rules.rationale: Schema 1.3 (ADR-030 / Migration 0003) makes nested language.content_locale (BCP 47) + root market the canonical locale path; root locale and defaults.locale are forbidden via additionalProperties: false. Wave 2 fix Q-WAVE1-F19-VALIDATOR-01 collapses pre-1.3 reads onto the 1.3 path only.

rules.rule: every events.jsonl line is < 64 KiB (events_writer cap)
rules.rationale: events_writer enforces a 64 KiB per-line cap so events.jsonl stays line-stream parseable on stdlib JSON readers; lines exceeding the cap indicate a writer bypass (rule append-only-state §3) and corrupt the audit-trail replay loop.

rules.rule: every cell value < 32767 chars (Excel/openpyxl hard limit)
rules.rationale: Excel's hard cell-value limit is 32 767 characters; openpyxl raises IllegalCharacterError above this. Cells at or over the cap mean upstream prose was not summarized; downstream master.xlsx writes will fail and DURUR-3 fires.

transaction.py keep-7 FIFO rotation invariant; exceeding the cap means the rotation step was skipped and disk pressure accumulates. auto_repair_available=true — surplus backups can be deleted oldest-first without data loss.

rules.rule: if any project's _state/workflows/ has a completed sf-crawl-orchestrator run, mcp-tool-registry.json MUST list 'sf' under servers
rules.rationale: v1.8 Phase 4 D-SF-01/D-SF-02 cross-sheet invariant: a workspace that has produced SF MCP crawl evidence MUST have the engine's tool registry advertising the 'sf' server, otherwise downstream sf-import handoff and tooling discovery (claude mcp list cross-check) silently desync. Mirrors Q-SF-MCP-PHASE-3-CLOSURE-FOLLOWUPS-01 schema-first catch — workflow state and registry advertisement must stay aligned. severity HIGH (not CRITICAL) per Manager spec — drift produces broken provenance lineage but does not corrupt master.xlsx.

rules.rule: .mcp.json mcpServers keys MUST equal mcp-tool-registry.json servers keys (sets comparison; ScraplingServer↔scrapling case-fold per D-SF-02 alignment)
rules.rationale: v1.9 Phase 2 D-V1.9-02 cross-sheet invariant — detects drift between .mcp.json transport config + mcp-tool-registry.json tool inventory. Orphan transport (.mcp.json server missing from registry) OR orphan inventory (registry server missing from .mcp.json) → FAIL. ScraplingServer (capital) in .mcp.json normalizes to scrapling (lowercase) in registry per D-SF-02 naming.md alignment. Category csr_mcp mirrors F-23 (the analogous .mcp.json↔registry MCP invariant): spec FE-1 proposed 'engine_consistency' but that value is NOT in consistency-report.schema.json's 8-category enum, so check_F_24 emits csr_mcp to keep the JSON registry aligned with the code's report category — see Q-V1.9-PHASE-2-WORKER-01.

rules.rule: if project.config.sf.mcp.enabled=true, project.config.schema_version MUST be >= '1.5' (Migration 0005 prerequisite)
rules.rationale: v1.9 Phase 3 D-V1.9-10 — defensive check enforcing schema version coherence. Migration 0005 (v1.4→v1.5) adds sf block; enabled=true on v1.4 is impossible per Migration 0005 lock but defensive check catches manual misconfiguration. Category csr_mcp (mirrors F-23/F-24, the analogous MCP invariants): the consistency-report.schema.json 8-category enum has no SF-specific bucket, so check_F_25 emits csr_mcp. Version comparison is integer-tuple (split on '.'), NOT lexicographic — correct past '1.10' (D-V1.9-10).
